es: Reconocer metáforas cotidianas (feel down, a warm welcome, time is running out, a bright idea), entender su significado no literal y valorar qué actitud transmiten en correos, reuniones y opiniones.

vocabulary.es: literal, al pie de la letra

teaching.en: When we finally reached the village, the owner gave us such a warm welcome that the long, tiring journey was forgotten at once.
teaching.es: Cuando por fin llegamos al pueblo, el dueño nos dio una bienvenida tan cálida que el largo y cansado viaje se olvidó al instante.
teaching.explanationEs: A warm welcome es una metáfora: la bienvenida no tiene temperatura, pero transmite afecto y cercanía.
segments: When we finally reached the village, the owner gave us such a
warm welcome that the long, tiring journey was forgotten at once.
teaching.audioText: When we finally reached the village, the owner gave us such a warm welcome that the long, tiring journey was forgotten at once.

teaching.en: After weeks of bad news she began to feel down, and even the simplest decisions seemed heavy to her.
teaching.es: Tras semanas de malas noticias empezó a sentirse decaída, y hasta las decisiones más simples le parecían pesadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Feel down y heavy traducen la tristeza como dirección hacia abajo y como peso; no hay caída ni peso reales.
segments: After weeks of bad news she began to feel down,
and even the simplest decisions seemed heavy to her.
teaching.audioText: After weeks of bad news she began to feel down, and even the simplest decisions seemed heavy to her.

teaching.en: Time is running out, and a flood of unanswered requests is making the whole department nervous about Friday's deadline.
teaching.es: Se está acabando el tiempo, y una avalancha de peticiones sin responder pone nervioso a todo el departamento por el plazo del viernes.
teaching.explanationEs: Time is running out imagina el tiempo como algo que se vacía; a flood of + plural indica una cantidad abrumadora.
segments: Time is running out, and a flood of unanswered requests
is making the whole department nervous about Friday's deadline.
teaching.audioText: Time is running out, and a flood of unanswered requests is making the whole department nervous about Friday's deadline.

teaching.en: Calling an idea bright is ordinary imagery, because light stands for intelligence, which is why Ana's bright plan impressed everybody.
teaching.es: Llamar brillante a una idea es una imagen corriente, porque la luz representa la inteligencia, y por eso el plan brillante de Ana impresionó a todos.
teaching.explanationEs: Imagery es el conjunto de imágenes que usamos al hablar; bright idea asocia la luz con la claridad mental.
segments: Calling an idea bright is ordinary imagery, because light stands
for intelligence, which is why Ana's bright plan impressed everybody.
teaching.audioText: Calling an idea bright is ordinary imagery, because light stands for intelligence, which is why Ana's bright plan impressed everybody.

teaching.en: After a week in Lima, Tom said the city is a jungle because every driver, vendor and pedestrian competes for the same small space.
teaching.es: Después de una semana en Lima, Tom dijo que la ciudad es una selva porque cada conductor, vendedor y peatón compite por el mismo espacio pequeño.
teaching.explanationEs: The city is a jungle es una metáfora: no hay árboles ni animales, pero la imagen transmite caos y competencia.
segments: After a week in Lima, Tom said the city is a jungle
because every driver, vendor and pedestrian competes for the same small space.
teaching.audioText: After a week in Lima, Tom said the city is a jungle because every driver, vendor and pedestrian competes for the same small space.

teaching.en: A writer chooses a metaphor to convey a feeling quickly, whereas a literal description would need several careful sentences to do the same.
teaching.es: Un escritor elige una metáfora para transmitir un sentimiento con rapidez, mientras que una descripción literal necesitaría varias frases cuidadosas para lo mismo.
teaching.explanationEs: Metaphor es lo figurado; literal es lo que significa exactamente lo que dicen las palabras.
segments: A writer chooses a metaphor to convey a feeling quickly, whereas a
literal description would need several careful sentences to do the same.
teaching.audioText: A writer chooses a metaphor to convey a feeling quickly, whereas a literal description would need several careful sentences to do the same.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sentido tienen «feel down» y «heavy heart» en el mensaje de Leo?

choices.text: He is sad and disappointed, so he asks for more time.
He is ill and tired, so he will stay in bed today.
He is angry about the budget, so he wants to leave.

feedback.es: Las dos expresiones hablan del ánimo, no del cuerpo: Leo está desanimado por el presupuesto y por eso pide aplazar el informe.

hint.es: Ninguna de las dos expresiones habla de peso físico ni de una caída: fíjate en el estado de ánimo.

origin.text: Leo wrote to his manager: 'I feel down today. The news about the budget has left me with a heavy heart, and I would like to finish the report tomorrow instead of tonight.'

prompt.es: Completa: «En cuanto salió la noticia, una avalancha de llamadas llegó a la oficina.»

feedback.es: A flood of + plural expresa una cantidad enorme que llega de golpe, como una inundación de llamadas.

hint.es: Es la palabra de la enseñanza que significa «inundación» y se usa para «muchísimas cosas a la vez».

origin.text: The moment the news was published, a ___ of calls hit the office. Nobody had expected so many, and the phones never stopped ringing.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su cálida bienvenida transmitió más que cualquier discurso.»

answer.text: Her warm welcome conveyed more than any speech

feedback.es: El sujeto es her warm welcome y conveyed lleva el significado de la metáfora: el afecto dice más que las palabras.

hint.es: Empieza con Her warm welcome y termina con la palabra speech.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué ayudó a la hermana de la narradora.

choices.text: A long phone call with her family at home.
The friendly way her neighbours received her.
The calm and sunny weather in her new town.

feedback.es: «A warm welcome» se refiere a la acogida de los vecinos: eso cambió su ánimo; la llamada y el tiempo no se citan como ayuda.

origin.audio: I called my sister last night. She has just moved abroad, and she sounded a little down. She told me she felt like a small boat in a big storm, and that her heart was heavy whenever she thought of home. Then her voice changed, because the neighbours had given her a warm welcome, and that made her first week easier.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase metafórica con su traducción natural.

pairs: Our neighbours gave us a warm welcome.

pairs.es: Nuestros vecinos nos acogieron con cariño.

pairs: The schedule is a jungle of meetings.

pairs.es: El horario es un caos enmarañado de reuniones.

pairs: A flood of orders arrived in December.

pairs.es: Llegó una avalancha de pedidos en diciembre.

pairs: He had a bright idea about the budget.

pairs.es: Tuvo una idea inteligente sobre el presupuesto.

feedback.es: Cada metáfora se traduce por su efecto: acogida afectuosa, caos, cantidad abrumadora e inteligencia.

pairs: Our neighbours gave us a warm welcome.

pairs.es: Nuestros vecinos nos acogieron con cariño.

pairs: The schedule is a jungle of meetings.

pairs.es: El horario es un caos enmarañado de reuniones.

pairs: A flood of orders arrived in December.

pairs.es: Llegó una avalancha de pedidos en diciembre.

pairs: He had a bright idea about the budget.

pairs.es: Tuvo una idea inteligente sobre el presupuesto.

prompt.es: Lee las tres frases del blog: ¿en cuál se usa «warm» en sentido literal?

choices.text: The welcome from the villagers.
The owner, who cooked every evening.
The room, heated all night long.

feedback.es: Solo la habitación tiene una temperatura real gracias a la calefacción; la bienvenida y el carácter afable del dueño son imágenes de afecto.

origin.text: Travel blog: 'The village gave us a warm welcome. Our room was warm because the heating was on all night. The owner, a warm and friendly man, cooked for us every evening.'

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué espera la directora de su equipo.

choices.text: Proposals that solve problems, not more complaints.
Detailed reports on every request she has received.
Silence from everybody until the board has decided.

feedback.es: Pide que cada problema llegue con «a bright idea»: espera soluciones, no más quejas; no pide informes ni silencio.

origin.audio: At Monday's meeting, our manager opened with a long silence. She said the department had become a jungle this month: every team was fighting for the same budget, and a flood of requests had landed on her desk. She added that time was running out before the board meets, and that she did not want to hear about another problem unless it came with a bright idea. Then she smiled and thanked us for our patience.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué actitud deja entender el tono de la directora.

choices.text: She is angry and holds the whole team responsible for it.
She is under pressure, but she still appreciates the team.
She is relaxed and believes the deadline can move.

feedback.es: El silencio inicial y las imágenes muestran presión, pero termina sonriendo y agradeciendo la paciencia: valora al equipo.

origin.audio: At Monday's meeting, our manager opened with a long silence. She said the department had become a jungle this month: every team was fighting for the same budget, and a flood of requests had landed on her desk. She added that time was running out before the board meets, and that she did not want to hear about another problem unless it came with a bright idea. Then she smiled and thanked us for our patience.

prompt.es: Completa: «Al oír la decisión, salió con el corazón encogido sin decir nada.»

feedback.es: A heavy heart es la colocación fija para la tristeza que pesa: no se dice «a weight heart» ni «a big heart».

origin.text: When she heard the decision, she said nothing. She simply picked up her bag and left the room with a ___ heart, as if the news were a weight that she could not put down, and her colleagues understood how disappointed she was.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura defiende la autora sobre las metáforas cotidianas?

choices.text: They are quick, but a literal description is clearer.
They are easy to use, but they show a lack of effort.
They are useful tools for expressing feeling quickly.

feedback.es: La autora contradice a los críticos: en dos palabras la metáfora comunica lo que una descripción literal tardaría un párrafo en decir.

origin.text: Critics often say that everyday metaphors are lazy. I disagree. When a colleague tells me she feels down, she conveys in two words what a literal description of her mood would need a whole paragraph to explain, and everybody understands her at once.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe la directora este correo a los equipos?

choices.text: To encourage the teams and collect ideas without adding pressure.
To warn the teams that they must work late until Friday.
To announce that the teams will receive fewer requests.

feedback.es: Reconoce el cansancio, descarta las horas extra y solo pide una idea pequeña: busca motivar y reunir propuestas sin presionar.

origin.text: Dear all, I know the last weeks have been a jungle, and a flood of requests has left many of you feeling down. I am not asking anyone to work late. I simply want each team to send me one bright idea by Friday, however small, so that we can decide before time runs out.

prompt.es: Completa: «El estudio era una selva durante la última semana del proyecto.»

feedback.es: Jungle es la metáfora del caos donde cada uno compite por hacerse oír (también se acepta zoo); no es una descripción de plantas.

origin.text: Everyone agreed that the studio was a ___ during the last week of the project: phones rang all day, every team wanted the same small space, and only the loudest people were heard.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso de despedida y elige qué deja entender la directora de Tom.

choices.text: That the project will continue without any change at all.
That his departure will be a real loss for the team.
That she is relieved because he is finally leaving.

feedback.es: Llamarlo «the heart of the team» y decir que la oficina se sentirá fría sin él implica que su marcha será una pérdida real.

origin.audio: When Tom left the company, his manager called him the heart of the team. She said the office would feel cold without him, and that his bright ideas had kept the project alive for years. Tom smiled, but he admitted that he felt heavy as he packed his things.

es: Distinguir símil (as…as, like), metáfora (X is a Y) y personificación (cosas que actúan como personas), formar cada una con sus estructuras y juzgar si una imagen es original o un tópico.

teaching.en: During exam week Tom is as busy as a bee, although he admits that this comparison is a cliché because everybody uses it.
teaching.es: Durante la semana de exámenes Tom está tan ocupado como una abeja, aunque admite que esa comparación es un tópico porque todo el mundo la usa.
teaching.explanationEs: As + adjetivo + as compara con algo típico de esa cualidad y forma un símil; si todos lo usan, es un cliché.
segments: During exam week Tom is as busy as a bee, although he
admits that this comparison is a cliché because everybody uses it.
teaching.audioText: During exam week Tom is as busy as a bee, although he admits that this comparison is a cliché because everybody uses it.

teaching.en: The storm roared like an angry lion, and the sound was so strong that it seemed to evoke a wild animal rather than weather.
teaching.es: La tormenta rugió como un león enojado, y el sonido era tan fuerte que parecía evocar un animal salvaje más que el tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Like + nombre también forma un símil; evoke significa despertar una imagen o un recuerdo en la mente del lector.
segments: The storm roared like an angry lion, and the sound was so
strong that it seemed to evoke a wild animal rather than weather.
teaching.audioText: The storm roared like an angry lion, and the sound was so strong that it seemed to evoke a wild animal rather than weather.

teaching.en: For Carlos the final exam is a mountain, and he must climb it patiently, step by step, without looking at the top.
teaching.es: Para Carlos el examen final es una montaña, y debe escalarla con paciencia, paso a paso, sin mirar la cima.
teaching.explanationEs: Metáfora: sin like ni as, afirma que una cosa es otra (X is a Y).
segments: For Carlos the final exam is a mountain, and he must
climb it patiently, step by step, without looking at the top.
teaching.audioText: For Carlos the final exam is a mountain, and he must climb it patiently, step by step, without looking at the top.

teaching.en: Poets often attribute human actions to objects, for example when the wind seems to whisper secrets to the trees at night.
teaching.es: Los poetas suelen atribuir acciones humanas a los objetos, por ejemplo cuando el viento parece susurrar secretos a los árboles por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Personificación: una cosa que no es humana hace algo humano (whisper); attribute = atribuir una cualidad o acción.
segments: Poets often attribute human actions to objects, for example when the
wind seems to whisper secrets to the trees at night.
teaching.audioText: Poets often attribute human actions to objects, for example when the wind seems to whisper secrets to the trees at night.

teaching.en: A careful reader learns to draw a distinction between a simile, which uses like or as, and a metaphor, which simply says that one thing is another.
teaching.es: Un lector atento aprende a establecer una diferencia entre un símil, que usa like o as, y una metáfora, que simplemente dice que una cosa es otra.
teaching.explanationEs: Draw a distinction between A and B = distinguir con precisión dos cosas parecidas.
segments: A careful reader learns to draw a distinction between a simile, which uses like
or as, and a metaphor, which simply says that one thing is another.
teaching.audioText: A careful reader learns to draw a distinction between a simile, which uses like or as, and a metaphor, which simply says that one thing is another.

teaching.en: When our teacher says that the wind whispers, she is using personification, not a simile, because nothing in the sentence is being compared.
teaching.es: Cuando nuestra profesora dice que el viento susurra, usa personificación y no un símil, porque en la frase no se compara nada.
teaching.explanationEs: Personification es la figura; el viento recibe una acción humana sin que haya comparación.
segments: When our teacher says that the wind whispers, she is using personification,
not a simile, because nothing in the sentence is being compared.
teaching.audioText: When our teacher says that the wind whispers, she is using personification, not a simile, because nothing in the sentence is being compared.

prompt.es: Clasifica la imagen principal del diario de Carlos.

choices.text: A simile: the exam is compared to a mountain with like.
A metaphor: the exam is said to be a mountain.
Personification: the mountain acts like a person.

feedback.es: El diario afirma que el examen es una montaña, sin like ni as: es una metáfora; la montaña no hace nada humano.

hint.es: Busca si aparece like o as, y si una cosa simplemente «es» otra.

origin.text: From Carlos's diary: 'This week the final exam is a mountain, and I am still at the start, looking up at a top that I cannot see through the clouds.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom se volvió tan ocupado como una abeja.»

feedback.es: As busy as a bee es el símil fijo de as + adjetivo + as; el adjetivo describe la cualidad típica de la abeja.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que describe a quien no para de trabajar.

origin.text: As soon as the exams began, Tom became as ___ as a bee: he studied at lunch, on the bus and even while he waited for his coffee.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Toda la ciudad duerme en silencio cuando cae la noche.»

answer.text: The whole city sleeps quietly when night falls

feedback.es: Es personificación: la ciudad hace algo humano, dormir; when night falls indica el momento.

hint.es: Sujeto + verbo humano + quietly + when night falls.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige qué figura prefiere la autora.

choices.text: The one that compares the noise with a machine.
The one that turns the sky into an artist.
The one that treats the storm as a character.

feedback.es: Prefiere la personificación porque convierte la tormenta en una persona; el símil del tren y la metáfora del pintor los presenta sin preferirlos.

origin.audio: In today's episode the writer compares three ways of describing a storm. First she says the storm was as loud as a train, which is a simile. Then she says the sky was an angry painter throwing grey paint everywhere, which is a metaphor. Finally she writes that the wind shouted at the village, and she explains that this is personification. She prefers the third, because it makes the storm feel like a person.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la figura que usa.

pairs: My brother is as quiet as a mouse in class.
The committee is a mountain of reports.
The old clock refused to work on Monday.
The committee meets every Tuesday morning.

feedback.es: El conector as…as marca el símil, «X is a Y» la metáfora, y un objeto que se niega a trabajar es personificación.

pairs: My brother is as quiet as a mouse in class.
The committee is a mountain of reports.
The old clock refused to work on Monday.
The committee meets every Tuesday morning.

prompt.es: Completa: «La tormenta golpeó el pueblo como un tren.»

feedback.es: Like + nombre forma el símil: delante de a train no se puede usar as, que se reserva para as…as o para funciones.

origin.text: The storm hit the town ___ a train, and for an hour nobody in the village dared to leave home.

prompt.es: Escucha a la profesora y elige qué frase del borrador es una metáfora.

choices.text: The one that says the exam simply is a mountain.
The one that compares the exam with climbing a mountain.
The one that says the mountain watches the students.

feedback.es: La frase que afirma que el examen es una montaña, sin conector, es la metáfora; comparar con escalar es un símil y la montaña que vigila es personificación.

origin.audio: Our teacher read three sentences from student drafts. The first said that the exam was as difficult as climbing a mountain. The second said that the exam was a mountain. The third said that the mountain was watching the students and waiting for them to make a mistake. She explained that only one of them is a metaphor, and she warned us that the third, although more original, risks sounding exaggerated if the topic is only a school test.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué implica la profesora sobre la tercera frase.

choices.text: It is wrong, because a mountain cannot act like a person.
It is original, but it may sound exaggerated for the topic.
It is the best, because exaggerated images always work well.

feedback.es: Reconoce su originalidad («more original»), pero avisa de que puede sonar exagerada para un simple examen.

origin.audio: Our teacher read three sentences from student drafts. The first said that the exam was as difficult as climbing a mountain. The second said that the exam was a mountain. The third said that the mountain was watching the students and waiting for them to make a mistake. She explained that only one of them is a metaphor, and she warned us that the third, although more original, risks sounding exaggerated if the topic is only a school test.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los poetas suelen atribuir sentimientos humanos a las cosas.»

feedback.es: Attribute X to Y es la colocación precisa para adjudicar una cualidad o emoción a algo; es la base de la personificación.

origin.text: Poets often ___ human feelings to things: when the sea is angry or the wind whispers, the writer is giving nature a human character of its own.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura defiende el autor sobre los símiles con as…as?

choices.text: Similes can be fresh, but the as…as pattern makes them predictable.
Teachers are mostly right: as…as similes rarely surprise anybody.
Similes are fine; predictable comparisons are the real problem.

feedback.es: El autor separa la estructura, que es válida, de la falta de ideas frescas: no culpa a los símiles, sino a las comparaciones previsibles.

origin.text: Some teachers say that every as…as simile is a cliché. I am not so sure. 'As busy as a bee' is tired, certainly, but 'as quiet as a library at midnight' still surprises the reader. The problem is not the structure; it is the lack of fresh ideas behind it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le pide la editora a Sam en su correo?

choices.text: To keep the jungle metaphor and renew the tired simile.
To keep both images and move the bee simile elsewhere.
To replace both images with literal descriptions of the office.

feedback.es: La editora elogia la metáfora de la selva y critica el símil de la abeja: pide conservar la primera y cambiar el segundo.

origin.text: Dear Sam, thank you for the draft. Your comparison of the office with a jungle was vivid, but 'as busy as a bee' in the next paragraph is a cliché and hurts it. Please keep the metaphor and replace the simile with a fresher image before Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «La profesora nos pidió establecer una diferencia entre símil y metáfora.»

feedback.es: Draw a distinction between A and B es la colocación formal para distinguir dos cosas (también se acepta draw a line); no se dice «make a difference» con este sentido.

origin.text: The teacher asked us to draw a ___ between a simile and a metaphor, that is, to say exactly how they differ, and most of the class found the exercise harder than we had expected.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota y elige qué deja entender la hablante sobre su hermana.

choices.text: That her sister was offended by the comparison with a fridge.
That her sister's image was funnier than her own.
That her own comparison was more original than her sister's.

feedback.es: Al admitir que la broma de su hermana era mejor que su comparación, deja entender que la imagen de la hermana era más ingeniosa.

origin.audio: I told my sister that her new flat was as cold as a fridge. She laughed and said that the old walls had complained all night. Then I realised that she had answered my simile with personification, and that her joke was better than my comparison.

title.en: Figurative language in sports and weather
title.es: Lenguaje figurado en deporte y clima

es: Interpretar el lenguaje figurado de una crónica deportiva, de un parte meteorológico y de una columna de opinión: localizar la expresión, explicar qué quiere decir en realidad y valorar la actitud del hablante.

teaching.en: City crushed United 3–0 on Saturday, and the radio commentary said that their defence was a wall that no striker could climb.
teaching.es: El City aplastó al United por 3–0 el sábado, y el comentario de la radio dijo que su defensa era un muro que ningún delantero podía escalar.
teaching.explanationEs: Crushed = ganó con mucha claridad; a wall = una defensa que nadie puede pasar. Commentary es el comentario en directo.
segments: City crushed United 3–0 on Saturday, and the radio commentary said
that their defence was a wall that no striker could climb.
teaching.audioText: City crushed United 3–0 on Saturday, and the radio commentary said that their defence was a wall that no striker could climb.

teaching.en: After the first goal the visitors looked like a sinking ship, and nothing their captain shouted seemed able to turn the tide.
teaching.es: Tras el primer gol los visitantes parecían un barco que se hunde, y nada de lo que gritó su capitán parecía capaz de cambiar el rumbo del partido.
teaching.explanationEs: A sinking ship = un equipo que se desmorona; turn the tide = invertir una situación adversa.
segments: After the first goal the visitors looked like a sinking ship,
and nothing their captain shouted seemed able to turn the tide.
teaching.audioText: After the first goal the visitors looked like a sinking ship, and nothing their captain shouted seemed able to turn the tide.

teaching.en: The second half was a rollercoaster, with three goals in ten minutes and a crowd that could hardly stay in their seats.
teaching.es: La segunda parte fue una montaña rusa, con tres goles en diez minutos y un público que apenas podía quedarse sentado.
teaching.explanationEs: A rollercoaster = muchas subidas y bajadas de emoción en poco tiempo.
segments: The second half was a rollercoaster, with three goals in ten
minutes and a crowd that could hardly stay in their seats.
teaching.audioText: The second half was a rollercoaster, with three goals in ten minutes and a crowd that could hardly stay in their seats.

teaching.en: The forecast says that a blanket of snow will cover the hills by midnight, so the outlook for the weekend is bleak.
teaching.es: El pronóstico dice que un manto de nieve cubrirá las colinas a medianoche, así que las perspectivas para el fin de semana son sombrías.
teaching.explanationEs: A blanket of snow = una capa que lo cubre todo; bleak describe un panorama poco esperanzador.
segments: The forecast says that a blanket of snow will cover the
hills by midnight, so the outlook for the weekend is bleak.
teaching.audioText: The forecast says that a blanket of snow will cover the hills by midnight, so the outlook for the weekend is bleak.

teaching.en: Storm clouds are gathering over the coast, which means that anyone planning a picnic should take an umbrella and avoid the beach.
teaching.es: Se están acumulando nubes de tormenta sobre la costa, lo que significa que quien planee un pícnic debería llevar paraguas y evitar la playa.
teaching.explanationEs: Are gathering personifica las nubes: se reúnen como personas; el sentido real es que va a llover.
segments: Storm clouds are gathering over the coast, which means that anyone
planning a picnic should take an umbrella and avoid the beach.
teaching.audioText: Storm clouds are gathering over the coast, which means that anyone planning a picnic should take an umbrella and avoid the beach.

teaching.en: By Friday the sun should chase the clouds away, although the forecast admits that this promise is not completely certain.
teaching.es: Hacia el viernes el sol debería ahuyentar las nubes, aunque el pronóstico admite que esa promesa no es del todo segura.
teaching.explanationEs: Chase away: el sol actúa como un perseguidor; el sentido real es que saldrá el sol.
segments: By Friday the sun should chase the clouds away, although
the forecast admits that this promise is not completely certain.
teaching.audioText: By Friday the sun should chase the clouds away, although the forecast admits that this promise is not completely certain.

prompt.es: Según la crónica, ¿qué significan «crushed» y «a wall»?

choices.text: A narrow win, with a goalkeeper who saved all the attacks.
A heavy loss, with defenders who left the door open.
A very clear win, with defenders who allowed no chances.

feedback.es: El marcador 4–0 y el dato de que los visitantes no tuvieron ninguna ocasión confirman una victoria clara y una defensa impenetrable.

hint.es: Fíjate en el marcador y en que los visitantes nunca tuvieron una ocasión de marcar.

es: Crear una metáfora, un símil y una personificación propios sobre un lugar o una estación, evitar los tópicos y explicar por qué cada imagen funciona en un texto breve y coherente.

origin.text: In a short text, every image has to stand ___, so avoid the expressions that everybody has already heard a thousand times and look for one that surprises the reader.

prompt.es: Describe un mercado lluvioso con metáfora, símil, personificación y explicación.

answer.text: On a rainy Saturday the market was a grey river. People moved between the stalls like leaves on the water, and the rain danced on the roofs and whispered to the fruit. The lamps were golden apples in the dark morning, and the whole place seemed to breathe warm air. I chose the river because it shows how the crowd never stops moving, even when the weather is bad. The sellers called their prices, and the smell of bread and coffee made everybody smile. A hint of sadness hung over the umbrellas, yet the noise was so cheerful that I forgot the cold. It was a noisy, colourful place, and I felt small in the middle of it, like a boat on the river.
accepted: On a rainy Saturday the market was a grey river. People moved between the stalls like leaves on the water, and the rain danced on the roofs and whispered to the fruit. The lamps were golden apples in the dark morning, and the whole place seemed to breathe warm air. I chose the river because it shows how the crowd never stops moving, even when the weather is bad. The sellers called their prices, and the smell of bread and coffee made everybody smile. A hint of sadness hung over the umbrellas, yet the noise was so cheerful that I forgot the cold. It was a noisy, colourful place, and I felt small in the middle of it, like a boat on the river.

Yesterday the market was a big kitchen on a rainy day. The sellers shouted like cooks, and the crowd moved as slowly as a river between the stalls. The rain danced on the umbrellas and sang a quiet song. The fruit looked like small lamps, red and yellow and green, and the smell of bread and coffee was a warm hug for everybody. I chose the kitchen because it shows how warm and busy the place was, even when the sky was grey. Everybody was wet, but everybody was smiling, and the market kept breathing until the evening. A hint of sugar and smoke stayed in my clothes when I finally walked home, and I did not mind at all.

feedback.es: Un buen texto mantiene una sola escena, combina las tres figuras y cierra con una frase que explica por qué funciona una de ellas.

origin.text: Describe un mercado en un día de lluvia. Escribe unas 130 palabras (mínimo 112) con una metáfora, un símil y una personificación que formen una sola escena, y explica en una frase por qué elegiste una de las imágenes.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la crítica principal de esta reseña del poema?

choices.text: The writer uses too many similes instead of metaphors.
The images are attractive but do not form one picture.

feedback.es: La reseña califica cada imagen de bonita, pero las sitúa en «three different places»: el problema es la falta de coherencia.

origin.text: Review: 'The writer calls autumn a painter, the leaves a carpet and the wind a dancer. Each image is pretty, but together they belong to three different places. The text would be stronger with only the painter, who could then mix the red, colour the trees and wait for the night to cover the work.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Elegí la palabra «espejo» porque muestra lo quieto que está el lago.»

feedback.es: I chose… because… es la fórmula para justificar una imagen; se usa el pasado chose, no el infinitivo choose.

origin.text: I ___ the word mirror because it shows how still the lake is, although a different writer might have preferred glass or silver for the same scene.

origin.audio: My brother described our old street in autumn. He said the houses were tired old men and the leaves were a golden carpet for their feet. I laughed, but I noticed that he had built one single picture, with old men and a carpet and feet, and that is why his description felt so vivid.

title.en: An extended metaphor in a personal essay
title.es: Metáfora extendida en un ensayo personal

es: Sostener una metáfora extendida en un ensayo personal sin mezclar imágenes: abrir con la metáfora, desarrollarla con elementos del mismo campo y cerrar con una reflexión que diga en sentido literal lo aprendido.

teaching.en: Learning English is a long journey, and every lesson is one more step along a road that I can only see a few metres ahead.
teaching.es: Aprender inglés es un largo viaje, y cada clase es un paso más por un camino del que solo veo unos pocos metros por delante.
teaching.explanationEs: Metáfora extendida: abres con la imagen (journey) y la sigues con elementos del mismo campo, como step.
segments: Learning English is a long journey, and every lesson is one more step
along a road that I can only see a few metres ahead.
teaching.audioText: Learning English is a long journey, and every lesson is one more step along a road that I can only see a few metres ahead.

teaching.en: Grammar is my map and vocabulary is my compass, so even when the road is unclear I can still find my direction.
teaching.es: La gramática es mi mapa y el vocabulario es mi brújula, así que aun cuando el camino no está claro puedo encontrar mi dirección.
teaching.explanationEs: Cada parte del aprendizaje recibe un elemento del viaje (map, compass): así la imagen se sostiene.
segments: Grammar is my map and vocabulary is my compass, so even
when the road is unclear I can still find my direction.
teaching.audioText: Grammar is my map and vocabulary is my compass, so even when the road is unclear I can still find my direction.

teaching.en: Sometimes I feel lost, but each mistake shows me where the road turns, and that helps me stay on course.

teaching.explanationEs: Sigues en el mismo campo: perdido, camino, giro, rumbo. Stay on course = no desviarte de tu objetivo.
segments: Sometimes I feel lost, but each mistake shows me where
the road turns, and that helps me stay on course.
teaching.audioText: Sometimes I feel lost, but each mistake shows me where the road turns, and that helps me stay on course.

teaching.en: To sustain a metaphor, choose one field and keep every new detail inside it, so that the essay remains coherent from the first line to the last.
teaching.es: Para sostener una metáfora, elige un campo y mantén cada detalle nuevo dentro de él, de modo que el ensayo sea coherente de la primera línea a la última.
teaching.explanationEs: Sustain = mantener algo a lo largo del tiempo; coherent = con todas las partes bien unidas.
segments: To sustain a metaphor, choose one field and keep every new detail inside it,
so that the essay remains coherent from the first line to the last.
teaching.audioText: To sustain a metaphor, choose one field and keep every new detail inside it, so that the essay remains coherent from the first line to the last.

teaching.en: If vocabulary is my compass but grammar is my sword, the image becomes mixed, and the reader wonders whether I am travelling or fighting.

origin.audio: To be honest, learning Spanish was like growing a garden. I planted a few words, watered them with practice and waited. For months nothing seemed to happen, and I almost gave up, because every week I compared myself with people who seemed to learn faster. Then, one morning, I understood a whole conversation on the bus, and I felt so happy that I wanted to tell everybody. Looking back, patience was the best water, although I did not know it then.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un día llegaré a mi destino, pero el camino ya me ha enseñado más.»

feedback.es: Reach + destination es la colocación natural para llegar a la meta; arrive necesitaría la preposición at.

origin.text: One day I will ___ my destination, but I already know that the road itself has taught me more than the arrival will.

prompt.es: Escribe un ensayo con una metáfora extendida sobre aprender un idioma.

answer.text: Learning English is a long journey. At the beginning I was standing at the door with no map, and I felt lost. Grammar became my map, and vocabulary became my compass. Every class was a step, and every mistake was a wrong turn that showed me a new direction. Sometimes the road was long and I walked slowly, but I never stopped. Now I can understand songs, films and conversations, and I am not afraid of wrong turns any more. I still stay on course because I practise every day, even when I am tired, and my friends walk beside me and help me laugh at every wrong turn. Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed. One day I will reach my destination, but the road itself is already a good place to live.
accepted: Learning English is a long journey. At the beginning I was standing at the door with no map, and I felt lost. Grammar became my map, and vocabulary became my compass. Every class was a step, and every mistake was a wrong turn that showed me a new direction. Sometimes the road was long and I walked slowly, but I never stopped. Now I can understand songs, films and conversations, and I am not afraid of wrong turns any more. I still stay on course because I practise every day, even when I am tired, and my friends walk beside me and help me laugh at every wrong turn. Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed. One day I will reach my destination, but the road itself is already a good place to live.

Learning English is a garden. On the first day I planted a few words, and every morning I watered them with a little practice. Some words grew quickly and others needed more time, but I never stopped planting. Grammar was the ground, and my mistakes were the bad plants that I took out one by one. My teacher was a patient gardener, and my friends were the sun. Sometimes it was hard, and I felt lost in the garden, but I stayed on course by returning every day. Looking back, the garden taught me that patience matters more than speed. Today I have a few flowers, and I am happy, but I will keep planting new words every day. In the end, the flowers did not come quickly, but they came, and I am proud of every single one of them.

feedback.es: Un buen ensayo abre con la metáfora, la desarrolla con elementos del mismo campo, incluye una dificultad y cierra con una reflexión literal.

origin.text: Escribe un ensayo de unas 140 palabras (mínimo 126) sobre aprender un idioma. Abre con una sola metáfora extendida (por ejemplo, un viaje), desarróllala con al menos tres elementos de esa imagen, incluye una dificultad y cierra con una reflexión (por ejemplo, con «Looking back»).

prompt.es: ¿Qué elemento rompe la imagen del jardín en este ensayo?

choices.text: Every mistake is a weed that I pull out.
I plant words and water them with practice.
My teacher is a train that never stops.

feedback.es: El tren no pertenece a un jardín; plantar, regar y arrancar malas hierbas sí mantienen la imagen.

origin.text: Essay: 'Learning English is a garden. I plant words, I water them with practice, and every mistake is a weed that I pull out. Lately, though, my teacher is a train that never stops, and I cannot keep up with it.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Una lección breve cada día me ayuda a mantener el rumbo.»

feedback.es: Stay on course significa no desviarte de tu objetivo durante el viaje; en una metáfora de viaje es el rumbo que mantienes (también se acepta stay on track).

origin.text: A short lesson every day helps me stay on ___, even when the road is long and I am tired.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué función cumple este cierre dentro del ensayo.

choices.text: It states in plain words what the writer learned.
It opens a second metaphor about a new experience.
It lists the steps needed to reach the destination.

feedback.es: El cierre resume la lección (confiar en el camino, seguir andando despacio) sin abrir otra imagen ni dar instrucciones.

origin.audio: Looking back, I see that the road was long, and that most of the time I did not know where I was going. But every wrong turn taught me something, and I now trust the road more than the map. I will keep walking, slowly, because that is what the journey has taught me.
